accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS N-CN.1 and AS Further Maths specifications (AQA 7366, Edexcel 8FM0): z = a + bi with a, b real, i² = −1, Re(z) = a and Im(z) = b (a real number), reals as the subset with b = 0, equality by equating real and imaginary parts. Every card checked: √(−9) = 3i (principal root), i² = −1 real, (1 + i) − i = 1, (1 + i) + (1 − i) = 2. The ambiguous case 0 (purely imaginary or not) is avoided and the adult note says why.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented errors: Im(z) written with the i (step 0 prediction, challenge tag imi, mastery m5), swapped real and imaginary parts (plane feedback for swapped points, tag swap, 2 + 3i vs 3 + 2i), reals not being complex (step 1 prediction, tag noi, m1), i² = 1 (tag sq, i² card), matching only one part (tag half, 3 − 2i vs 3 + 2i), and thinking one equation cannot find two unknowns (step 2 prediction, tag one).

lab_distinct.evidence: Mechanisms are specific to ℂ: a draggable point on the complex plane that reads out Re(z) and Im(z) and diagnoses swapped or sign-flipped placements, a Venn-style ℂ box with real and purely imaginary regions, steppers for x and y with live real-part and imaginary-part comparisons, and standard-form rewriting. Gate similarity under 30% to all flagship labs, including flagcxroot.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each rule by acting: misplaced points name the exact slip, sorting shows that every number lands somewhere inside ℂ, the solver turns each part green only when it matches so two equations appear naturally, and wrong standard forms explain the step that went wrong.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: Im(4 − 7i) = '−7i', '5 has no i so it is not complex', and 'one equation cannot give two unknowns'.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with tagged distractors: imi (Im is real, no i), swap (real part first, coefficient of i second), noi and neg (every real is a + 0i), one (equal parts give two equations), real and both (purely imaginary needs a = 0), sq (i² = −1), half (both parts must match).

readability.evidence: Kid text FK grade 4.4 and adult 6.5 (limits 6.5 and 9.5). Notation Re(z), Im(z) and ℂ is introduced with a worked example (4 − 7i) before it is used.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed. The four kid paragraphs cover why i exists, the two parts, how ℝ and the purely imaginary numbers sit in ℂ, and equality. Explanation under 12% similar to lesson 928 (complex roots of quadratics).

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of every step (/workspace/wn-run-1116-1351/shots/cx-*). The plane is a full-width square with labelled axes and a 48 px drag target, the ℂ regions fit three across at 390 px with wrapped labels, the x and y steppers are large +/− tiles, and the three answer tiles in the form step use 18 px text.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five tasks complete with Show me, challenge shown, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes, no console errors. Buttons cover every action (real/imaginary part ±1 and Check, sort boxes, x and y ±1, answer choices) and the canvas aria-label reads the target, the point's real and imaginary parts, or both sides' parts in the solver.
